outlooks.summary: Scattered severe thunderstorms are expected this afternoon and evening from parts of south-central Texas to the Coastal Plain with damaging wind and large hail. Scattered strong to severe storms are also anticipated from Salt Lake northward across the Upper Snake River Plain and into central Montana, and during the day over central Mississippi where a tornado is possible.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: A low-amplitude shortwave trough will move east across TX during the day, approaching the Lower MS Valley by 12Z Friday. Mid to upper-level westerlies will average 40-70 kt respectively, enhancing deep-layer shear profiles. At the surface, a stalled front will stretch from a low near the ArkLaMiss southwestward toward Austin/San Antonio, with western portions of the front possibly enforced by early day outflow. A very moist air mass will reside south of these boundaries with dewpoints into the 70s F. To the west, a stronger upper trough will move across the Pacific Northwest, with low pressure deepening over eastern MT. A cold front will extend from central MT into NV during the day, with a few severe storms expected along and ahead of it as lift increases through the period.

sections.title: Central TX to the middle Coastal Plain
sections.text: A fast-moving line of storms will move across central TX early in the morning with the outflow likely stalling during the day. Strong heating upstream over the Rio Grande Valley along with 70s F dewpoints south of the front will result in strong instability. Increased mid to upper winds around the base of the upper trough will lengthen hodographs, but low-level winds will be weak. Thus, a rightward-propagating MCS is possible, and indeed forecast by several CAMs during the early to mid afternoon forming along the boundary and moving toward the middle TX Coast. Damaging winds will be the main threat, followed by large hail with non-linear storm modes.

sections.title: Southeast LA...southern MS...southwest AL
sections.text: A very moist air mass with mid 70s F dewpoints will spread northward behind a warm front which will reach I-20 by early afternoon. Meanwhile, wind profiles will strengthen a bit, in advance of the shortwave trough to the west. Southwesterly 850 mb winds of 30-40 kt are forecast which will enlarge hodographs near the warm front. Some uncertainty exists regarding the degree of air mass contamination via early day precipitation, but embedded supercells will still be possible due to mid 70s F dewpoints.

sections.title: Northern UT into central MT
sections.text: Cooling aloft with the upper trough and heating will steepen lapse rates, resulting in around 1000 J/kg MUCAPE ahead of the cold front from northern UT into MT. Winds aloft will also increase, with 40-50 kt EBS supporting both cells and bowing structures. Cold temperatures aloft will favor hail, while deep mixed layers below 700 mb favor damaging winds. ..Jewell/Bentley.. 06/06/2019

outlooks.summary: The greatest potential for severe thunderstorms will be over parts of south-central and southeast Texas this afternoon, with severe winds and large hail expected. Other severe storms are possible over parts of the northern Rockies region and from the lower Mississippi Delta region to western Alabama.

sections.title: Southeastern LA and Southern MS
sections.text: Tornado probabilities have been increased across southeastern LA and southern MS where a couple low-level circulations embedded within a line have produced reports of damage, likely associated with tornadoes based on dual-pol radar data. For more information, see Mesoscale Discussion 1003 and Tornado Watch 335. The previous discussion from 13Z follows.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: Inland movement and amplification of synoptic troughing over the Northwest will contribute to a more-progressive version of the longstanding split-flow pattern downstream. A cyclone associated with that synoptic trough -- now apparent in moisture-channel imagery centered near then northwestern tip of Vancouver Island, is forecast to weaken within the broader cyclonic flow field. Meanwhile, the trough should penetrate inland to southeastern BC, central WA/OR and northern CA by the end of the period. Meanwhile, a southern-stream trough that resided over the Southwest for several days has ejected to the southern High Plains, and will move slowly eastward across portions of TX/OK through this evening. The central vorticity max and intermittently closed 500-mb low will move roughly along I-40 from its present position over the TX Panhandle, across OK to central AR by 12Z, by which time the trough should extend south-southwestward over the northwestern Gulf. At the surface, 11Z analysis showed a wavy, diffuse frontal zone from southern New England and the inland Mid-Atlantic region to central/western IL, through a weak low over southwestern IA, to another low over northwestern OK. sections.title: South-central/southeast TX
sections.text: Severe hail and wind are expected from thunderstorms developing this afternoon near SAT and expanding/shifting east-southeastward to parts of the middle/upper TX Coast. The outflow boundary should stall and probably retreat somewhat northward through this afternoon, before aiding in widely scattered to scattered thunderstorm development this afternoon near the western rim of the outlook area. Storms should grow upscale while impinging on a very moist, high-theta-e, weakly capped environment near and south of the boundary, toward the middle/upper TX Coast. Steep low/midlevel lapse rates atop 70s F surface dew points will yield 3500-4000 J/kg MLCAPE along and south of the boundary. Initial supercellular mode may occur, favoring large hail and damaging gusts. The severe-wind threat will become more dominant and well-organized with time and eastward extent as upscale evolution occurs, with potential for cold-pool development/reinforcement and forward propagation astride the outflow boundary. sections.title: LA/MS/AL
sections.text: A few tornadoes are possible today within a plume of scattered thunderstorms moving eastward to northeastward across the area. Isolated damaging wind also may occur. The 12Z LIX sounding sampled a very moist low-level with surface dew points in the mid 70s F, PW exceeding 2 inches and mean mixing ratio around 19 g/kg. The favorably moist boundary layer will spread northeastward through the day in step with inland penetration of the warm front, while the low moves to western AL by 00Z. The high theta-e will offset modest midlevel lapse rates enough for 1000-2000 J/kg MLCAPE, amidst slight strengthening of the low-level flow above the surface. That trend, along with relatively backed flow near the surface low and warm front, will support supercell potential through enlarged low-level shear, with effective SRH in the 200-300 J/kg range. Uncertainty remains regarding inland penetration of the optimal air mass, given ongoing precip over the region, so mesoscale details may compel some reshaping of the outlook area (especially on the northern end) through the day.

sections.title: Northern Rockies and MT High Plains
sections.text: Widely scattered to scattered thunderstorms are expected to form within a southwest/northeast-aligned corridor this afternoon, individually moving northeastward as the entire regime shifts across the outlook area. Damaging gusts and large hail are the main concerns. As the northwestern mid/upper-level trough moves inland, height falls and corresponding strengthening of mid/upper southwesterlies are expected across the region through this evening, along with shots of DCVA related to small/ejecting perturbations in that flow aloft. The low-level response to these processes will include warm/moisture advection, cyclogenesis and frontogenesis, all combining with diurnal heating to contribute to increased lift at multiple scales. This will support organized thunderstorm development initially over portions of central/southwestern MT near the front in slightly more-favorable moisture/heating, then in a zone of deep low-level lift over southeastern ID/northern UT, across the I-15 corridor and into portions of western WY, including the Yellowstone/Teton park areas. outlooks.summary: The greatest potential for severe thunderstorms will be over parts of south-central and southeast Texas this afternoon, with severe winds and large hail expected. Other severe storms are possible over parts of the northern Rockies region and from the lower Mississippi Delta region to western Alabama.

sections.title: LA/MS
sections.text: An ongoing cluster of embedded supercell thunderstorms is affecting parts of southeast LA. Several mesocyclones have been noted in this cluster, and will likely continue for a few more hours as the storms track eastward. Regional VAD profiles confirm that low-level shear profiles remain favorable, and a very moist air mass is in place. Greater uncertainty exists farther north across parts of central MS. Short-term trends suggest the complex of storms will track into southeast AL and stay south of the area. However, some clearing has been noted over central MS where a very moist low-level environment is present. It appears possible that a few rotating storms may be able to develop this afternoon over east-central MS. The SLGT risk area has been adjusted accordingly.

sections.title: South-central and Southeast TX
sections.text: A slow moving upper low is currently over central OK, with an associated band of moderately strong westerly flow aloft extending across central TX. Models are surprisingly consistent on the development of intense thunderstorms over the risk area this afternoon, with storms increasing in coverage and intensity as they track eastward toward the coast. Initial supercell structures are expected, with a trend toward bowing structures as the storms move east. Have not made any changes to the risk area in this region.

sections.title: UT/WY/ID/MT
sections.text: Water vapor loop shows a strong and progressive upper trough moving into western OR. Lift ahead of this feature will overspread much of the northern Rockies this afternoon. Strong heating, steep lapse rates, and sufficient low level moisture will contribute to the development of scattered thunderstorms from northeast NV/northern UT into eastern ID/western WY. Sufficient CAPE, strong southwesterly flow aloft along the corridor, and steep low-level lapse rates, will promote a risk of damaging wind gusts and hail in the more intense storms. Farther west and later this afternoon, it appears likely that thunderstorms will develop over parts of western ID and track rapidly northeastward into western MT. Several model solutions suggest bowing structures capable of damaging winds. These storms will track into central MT after dark. ..Hart/Wendt.. 06/06/2019

outlooks.summary: The greatest potential for severe thunderstorms this afternoon and evening remains over parts of south-central and southeast Texas, with severe winds and large hail expected. Other, more isolated severe storms are possible over parts of the northern Rockies/High Plains, and from the lower Mississippi Delta region to western Alabama.

sections.title: 20Z Update
sections.text: Although the environment remains conditionally favorable for rotating storms across southern MS/AL in the short term, it remains unclear whether recent shower development over southeastern MS will be able to strengthen in the wake of morning convection. The 30-35 kt low-level jet over this region is forecast to gradually weaken and shift eastward later this evening. Even so, at least some risk for a brief tornado and/or strong wind gusts persists across this region. See Mesoscale Discussion 1007 for more information. Very minor changes have been made to the Slight/Enhanced risk areas across parts of southeast TX to account for current observational trends. Additional convective development should occur across the Hill County and along an outflow boundary across south TX from storms earlier this morning. For more information on the short-term severe threat across this region, see Mesoscale Discussion 1006. The Marginal and Slight risk areas have been expanded southward across parts of northern/central UT and eastern NV based on radar trends. mesoscale_discussions.summary: Threat for damaging wind gusts and tornadoes is increasing and tornado watch will be needed soon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Recent radar trends have shown an increase in updraft strength and rotation with the supercells embedded within the convective line moving across southeast LA. Mesoanalysis estimates over 2000 J/kg of MLCAPE exists ahead of this line, promoted by a very moist air mass characterized by dewpoints in the mid to upper 70s. Southerly/south-southeasterly surface winds ahead of the line are also relatively strong, with 20 kt reported at several stations south of the Lake Pontchartrain. Recent VAD profiles from both LIX and MOB show 20+ kt of 0-1 km vertical shear and over 100 m2/s2 of 0-1 km storm-relative helicity. Given the current trends and favorable downstream air mass, a tornado watch will likely be needed soon.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Threat for water-loaded downbursts and brief tornadoes will continue across southern AL/MS and the western/central FL Panhandle for the next few hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Thunderstorm coverage and intensity has trended downward across southeast LA over the past hour or so while persistent redevelopment offshore and resultant training has led to continued thunderstorm activity across southern AL. Over the past hour or so, the most intense storms have been predominantly over far southeast LA where a theta-e maximum was co-located with southerly/southeasterly surface winds and strong surface vorticity. Threat for water-loaded downbursts and brief tornadoes will continue across southern AL/MS and the western/central FL Panhandle but increasing displacement from the better low to mid-level flow (currently extending from southeast LA into central MS) and less instability suggests more isolated events than experienced over southeast LA. ..Mosier.. 06/06/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Storm will likely initiate/increase in coverage in the next 2-3 hours. Damaging wind gusts and large hail will be the primary threats. Greater storm organization will occur in northwest Wyoming vicinity with deep-layer shear maximized here with diminishing magnitudes farther southwest. A WW is possible in the next 1-2 hours for parts of the area.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A few elevated thunderstorms are ongoing in the discussion area. Areas away from this activity are receiving full sunshine with dewpoints holding in the low to upper 40s F. Guidance has tended to be too low with both temperatures and dewpoints this morning. That being said, buoyancy may reach the higher end of the expected 500-1000 J/kg range later this afternoon. 12Z SLC/LKN/RIW observed soundings showed near 8 C/km mid-level lapse rates and cold temperatures aloft which would support a threat of large hail. Strong surface heating will increase low-level lapse rates amidst relatively large temperature/dewpoint spreads at the surface making damaging convective gusts another concern. The overall severe threat will be maximized in northern portions of the discussion area where better deep-layer shear will exist. Cumulus development is already occurring on the higher terrain and scattered storm initiation will likely occur in the next 2-3 hours with continued surface heating and the approach of a weak mid-level perturbation moving northeast out of central California (per water vapor imagery). A WW is possible in the next 1-2 hours for parts of the area.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Environment is conditionally supportive of damaging wind gusts and isolated hail if storm develop. Trends will be monitored for additional convective initiation and the resulting need for a watch.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Visible satellite imagery has shown a building cumulus field across the TX Hill Country for the past hour or so as temperatures climb into the upper 80s/low 90s amidst upper 60s/low 70s dewpoints. Modifying recent RAP soundings with current observations suggests little to no convective inhibition remains. This erosion of the convective inhibition is also confirmed by the deeper convective development over Kerr County. Warm and dry mid-level conditions suggest that it could still be a hour or two before the air mass is conducive to more than isolated storm coverage. Even then, storm longevity will likely be impacted by the development of strong downdrafts and overall uncertainty regarding thunderstorm coverage leads to lower watch probability. That being said, any of the more persistent/robust storms could produce damaging wind gusts and isolated hail. Trends will be monitored for additional convective initiation and the resulting need for a watch.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Conditional risk for damaging wind gusts and brief tornadoes. Limited storm coverage may temper the need for a watch but convective trends will be monitored closely.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: 19Z surface analysis places a low over Vicksburg, MS on the central LA/MS border. Another low exists farther northeast over far southeast AR with a somewhat diffuse warm front extending eastward from the low into central MS and then eastward/southeastward through central AL. Visible imagery shows partly cloudy skies across MS. Resultant filtered diurnal heating has allowed temperatures to climb into the mid 80s amidst low/mid 70s dewpoints. More cloud cover has persistent thus far over areas farther downstream (i.e. west-central AL) with temperatures still in the upper 70s/low 80s. Even with these warm and humid conditions, instability will be limited by warm temperatures and poor lapse rates. Consequently, given this limited instability, dry mid-levels, and lack of stronger large-scale forcing for ascent, deep convection may struggle to persist. Given the favorable low-level vertical shear profiles, any more persistent/robust storms would likely have an associated risk for damaging wind gusts and brief tornadoes. Current expectation is for limited storm coverage to temper the need for a watch but convective trends will be monitored closely.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Storm initiation is likely in the next hour or two. Scattered severe thunderstorms will be possible with an attendant risk of large hail and damaging wind gusts. Storms may grow upscale into an MCS and pose more of damaging wind gusts threat later this afternoon. A WW is possible in the next two hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Visible satellite shows increasing cumulus development across the Bitterroot and vicinity with a couple upstream mid-level waves approaching southwestern Montana on water vapor imagery. While moisture will be limited (dewpoints in the mid 40s to perhaps near 50 F), strong surface heating has pushed temperatures into the mid to upper 80s F across portions of southwestern and central Montana. A modestly buoyant (MLCAPE of 500-1000 J/kg, greater values with eastward extent) airmass and steep mid-level lapse rates of 7.5-8.5 C/km will support storms capable large hail. Storms should initially be discrete with 40-55 kts of effective deep-layer shear. Inverted V low-level thermodynamic profiles will also support the threat for damaging wind gusts. Given how efficient outflow production will likely be as well as a tendency to have several splitting storms interact (long, generally straight hodographs), upscale growth into an MCS later this afternoon will be possible. Should an MCS develop, strong deep-layer flow parallel to storm motion would support a wider threat of damaging wind gusts. A WW may be needed in the next two hours.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The threat for damaging wind, hail, and perhaps a brief tornado or two will spread southeastward into this evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: At 2230Z, a cluster of intense thunderstorms over central TX is moving southeastward toward the southwestern Houston metro area. Other thunderstorms are developing further south in the vicinity of a surface boundary that has been pushing slowly northwestward during the day. Very warm and moist conditions are supporting very strong buoyancy, with MLCAPE of 3000-4000 J/kg in place per objective mesoanalyses and modified forecast soundings. Effective shear of 40-50 kt is more than sufficient for storm organization, with both supercells and upscale-growing segments possible into this evening. As these storms spread east-southeastward with time, damaging wind will likely become the primary threat, given the very warm/moist boundary layer and steep low-level lapse rates downstream of ongoing convection, with some cold pool generation/propagation possible as upscale growth occurs. Warm temperatures aloft will tend to limit a more substantial hail threat, though any supercell structures will remain capable of producing at least marginally severe hail. While low-level flow is weak, a brief tornado or two will also be possible with any supercell in the vicinity of the modified sea breeze boundary where surface winds are locally backed. ..Dean.. 06/06/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: High-based storms will continue to be capable of 60-70mph gusts across northeast MT early this evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Latest surface analysis indicates temperature-dewpoint spreads across northeast MT are 50-55 degrees F. The 00z Glasgow, MT raob showed a very deep boundary layer (inverted-V profile) with around 500 J/kg MLCAPE. Around 25kt 0-6km shear was sampled by the raob which would indicate some storm organization with the cold pool. The strongest thunderstorm core may be capable of sporadic occurrences of 1 inch diameter hail but the main risk with this activity will be 60-70mph gusts. ..Smith.. 06/06/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Transient supercells will be capable of intermittent strengthening of low-level mesocyclones with the strongest updrafts. A brief/weak tornado is possible this evening. The isolated character and magnitude of the threat will probably preclude the need for a small tornado watch.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Radar mosaic shows a band of convection, from north-central MS southeastward into west-central AL, with embedded discrete cores immediately east of a surface low over east-central MS. Surface observations show backed southeasterly surface winds east of the ongoing convective activity. KBMX VAD show the low-level winds acting to enlarge the hodograph (around 200 m2/s2 0-1km SRH). The 00z Birmingham, AL raob showed a very moist/deep boundary layer with just over 100 J/kg MLCAPE, all located below 500mb. The equilibrium level (based on a 100mb mean parcel) is just below the -20 degrees C level and would likely not support much lightning with the stronger updrafts. The moist-adiabatic lapse rate/pseudo tropical profile will not cool substantially during the evening. As a belt of modestly strong, southerly 850mb flow shifts northward across central and then into north-central AL and northwest GA through the late evening, expecting episodic strengthening of small mesocyclones in the very moist airmass over far east-central MS in the near term and later into parts of central AL. A brief/weak tornado may accompany the strongest circulations.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe threat will move offshore after 02Z, but damaging wind and localized hail threat will continue until then, especially with intense supercell southwest of Corpus Christi.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: At 01Z, thunderstorms have consolidated into a primarily linear mode (with embedded supercell structures) across the middle/upper TX coast, while an intense supercell is ongoing southwest of Corpus Christi. Some damaging wind threat will persist with the line, though the tendency has been for outflow to become increasingly dominant and for updrafts to gradually weaken with time as storms encounter increasing MLCINH near the coast. Further southwest, a 77 MPH wind gust was noted in the last hour with the supercell that passed near Kingsville, TX. The threat for widespread damaging wind and some hail should continue with this cell until it moves offshore by 02Z. ..Dean.. 06/07/2019 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...
